newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq puts probable oil reserves at 200 bln barrels.
newsitem.headline: Iraq puts probable oil reserves at 200 bln barrels.

text.p: Iraqi studies suggest that the country has probable oil reserves of 200 billion barrels, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya reported on Sunday.

"Studies indicate that probable (Iraqi) oil reserves are estimated at 200 billion barrels in addition to 112 billion barrels of proven oil reserves," Iraq's oil undersecretary Fa'iz Abdullah Shaheen told the paper.

He said oil excavations conducted by the oil ministry during the last few years had led to the discovery of new oil reserves. Shaheen said some of the new oilfields were located in Ammara 366 km (220 miles) south of Baghdad, Ukaz oilfield in southern Iraq and Bye Hassan in Kirkuk 255 km (155 miles) north of the capital.
Previously Iraqi officials have declared that Iraq's oil reserves could total 214 billion barrels.
Shaheen said the ministry planned also to raise its oil production capacities and talks were being held with international firms to improve Iraq's oilfields.

Iraq is banned by the United Nations from exporting its oil to the international markets as a punishment for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Under an oil-for-food deal signed with the U.N., on December 10 Iraq started limited oil sales worth $2 billion to buy urgent necessities for the Iraqi population.

Baghdad on Tuesday complained to the U.N. Security Council that food and medical supplies under the pact were taking too long to arrive while U.N. and U.S. officials said Iraq was blocking operations on the ground.
Prior to U.N. sanctions Iraq exported more than 2.5 million barrels per day.
